method: We first observed the technologies depicted in the paintings, such as airplanes, lights, microphones and fans, then considered the technologies behind their creation, such as industrially manufactured canvas and brushes. This method linked visual content with production processes.
results_discussion: I watched a clip from 2001: A Space Odyssey. It was inspired by a short story about human isolation in space. The movie use continuous silence, occasional beeps and extensive narration to emphasize that the character is the only human. His difficult entry into the "logic memory room" suggests a wish to reunite with humanity, yet the dominant red shows eternal isolation and danger. I thought his vertical movement as emotional expression, but later learned the staff use low-angle shots to hide the actor's steel cable. I have watched Kubrick's another film. He built a practical sets, a full New York street and in this film he use a huge centrifuge, these show his preference for in-camera effects over CGI. This really fascinates me.
title: W1
introduction: In the first week, we appreciated two paintings in class, and listened to audio recordings after class. These activities encouraged us to think about how art is supported by technology. This helped frame our initial reflections and inspired our creative thinking.
